title:
Competitive AI Safety is
the loss function to make sure AI goes well
primary_claim: seq2feature, a 5.3MB text-only probe distilled from a Gemma-2-9B SAE, recovers the SAE's concept readout from output text alone with 0.956 top-5 concept agreement and 0.90 per-concept AUC, beating bag-of-words (0.84/0.75) and zero-shot embedding (0.23/0.53) baselines, while running on CPU and degrading legibly out of distribution.
quote: My seq2feature 5.3MB text-only probe reproduces 90% of the capability of an SAE on held out text.
metric: top-5 concept agreement with SAE ground truth / per-concept AUC
target_value: 0.956 top-5 agreement, 0.90 AUC (seq2feature int8, 5.3MB) vs 0.84/0.75 bag-of-words, 0.23/0.53 embedding baseline, 1.00/1.00 SAE teacher
tolerance_rationale: headline is a compound of 12 numbers; compare the components by hand
inspector_notes: Best case in this batch: the exact headline metrics reproduce on CPU in minutes from data already committed to the repo. The only compute/API-heavy step in the whole project -- running the Gemma-2-9B teacher + GemmaScope SAE to generate ground-truth labels (README: needs an A100/80GB) and captioning 2048 concepts via Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite (~$0.80, needs OPENROUTER_KEY) -- is a one-time upstream step whose outputs (relabels.jsonl, targets.npz) are already shipped and not required to reproduce the reported numbers.
headline_artifact: notebooks/02_evaluate_probe.ipynb primary figure and printed summary -- per-concept AUC (0.90) and top-5 agreement (0.956) vs bag-of-words (0.84/0.75) and zero-shot embedding (0.23/0.53) baselines
